fixes.explanation: Wealth? Baker, I'm standing on a gold base and even I wouldn't say that's the point. The LORD says He raised Pharaoh up "…that I might display My power to you…" (Exodus 9:16). Power is the word, and it's not about money. Pharaoh is about to see exactly what that power looks like.

Laws, friend? That would be like me walking into my bakery and handing out a rulebook instead of cookies. Not this verse. The LORD says He raised Pharaoh up "…that I might display My power to you…" (Exodus 9:16). Laws never come up, and power does.

Thunder and lightning, baker! The sky went full drum solo with a light show on top. The text says, "The hail fell and the lightning continued flashing through it." (Exodus 9:24) Moses only stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the LORD sent the rest.

Wind and darkness, friend? That sounds like my old junk drawer on a quiet night. This sky was loud and flashing. The text says the LORD sent "…thunder and hail, and lightning struck the earth." (Exodus 9:23) Thunder and lightning are what came with the hail.

Canaan is a real place, baker, but this passage never mentions it. Egypt gets pounded, and the one spot the hail skipped is "…the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived." (Exodus 9:26) Picture the whole country under that storm and one patch the hail just walks around. That patch is Goshen.

Midian is a fine name, friend, but you won't find it in this passage. Look at what the verse says: "The only place where it did not hail was in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived." (Exodus 9:26) Everywhere else in Egypt took it. Goshen was the one place the hail left alone.

Far away? Baker, I think that's the last thing Pharaoh is feeling with thunder rattling his whole country. He doesn't say it. He says, "The LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked." (Exodus 9:27) He calls the LORD righteous, and he calls himself and his people wicked.

Heal the livestock? Friend, that sounds like a reasonable ask after a storm like that, but it's not what Pharaoh says. He wants the sky to stop: "Pray to the LORD, for there has been enough of God’s thunder and hail." (Exodus 9:28) His request is for prayer. Moses answers that he will spread out his hands to the LORD (Exodus 9:29).
